subject.title: fix(mcp): keep servers whose tool schemas omit a root type

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally accept MCP tool declarations that omit the protocol-required root `type: "object"`, or should it retain the current protocol contract and pursue an upstream SDK/spec change instead?
rationale: The linked server uses valid general JSON Schema composition, but the MCP protocol and current SDK explicitly require a root object type; choosing to relax that boundary is a compatibility policy decision that cannot be resolved mechanically.

options.title: Keep the MCP contract
options.body: Reject untyped root schemas as today and pursue any broader schema-shape change through the MCP specification or SDK.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded compatibility exception
options.body: Accept only schemas proven object-only through an SDK-supported parsing path that retains output-validator and task-support metadata.

recommendation.title: Keep the MCP contract
recommendation.body: Reject untyped root schemas as today and pursue any broader schema-shape change through the MCP specification or SDK.
